title: Recurring invoices and subscriptions
summary: Billing the same customer the same amount on a schedule, without remembering to do it.
html:
There are two ways to bill repeatedly, and they answer different questions.

  • A recurring invoice copies an existing invoice on a schedule. Use it for retainers and fixed monthly fees where the amount is the same every time.
  • A subscription is a product a customer is signed up to, with a renewal date and optionally an automatic payment. Use it when the customer is subscribing to something rather than being re-billed for work.

Both depend on the scheduled task running. Nothing recurs on its own — if invoices stop appearing, check the cron job before anything else.

Setting up a recurring invoice

Create the invoice once, then set it to recur: choose the interval and the date of the next one. On that date the scheduled task creates a fresh copy with new dates and a new number, leaving the original alone.

Whether a recurring invoice is renewed when the previous one is still unpaid is controlled by invoice_auto_renew_only_paid_invoices. Switching it on stops an unpaid customer quietly accumulating invoices.

Subscriptions

A subscription attaches a product to a customer with a renewal period. When it falls due, the scheduled task generates the invoice, and — if you have a gateway that supports it — can take the payment automatically.

subscription_merge_invoices controls whether several subscriptions falling due for the same customer on the same day become one invoice or several. One is usually what the customer wants.

Stopping one

Cancelling a subscription or switching off a recurring invoice stops the next one being created. It does not touch invoices already raised; cancel those with a credit note if they should not have gone out.
